'''''Ptychostomum pseudotriquetrum''''', commonly known as '''marsh bryum''',<ref>{{Cite web|title=''Bryum pseudotriquetrum'', Marsh Bryum|url=https://species.nbnatlas.org/species/NHMSYS0000309510|access-date=11 February 2022|website=[[NBN Atlas]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Marsh Bryum names - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/924223/names|access-date=11 February 2022|website=[[Encyclopedia of Life]]}}</ref> is a species of [[moss]] belonging to the family [[Bryaceae]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Ptychostomum pseudotriquetrum'' (Hedw.) J.R. Spence & H.P. Ramsay ex Holyoak & N. Pedersen |url=http://www.worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-0001176868 |website=[[World Flora Online]] |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref>  It is distinguished by its strongly [[decurrent]] leaves that extend down the stem, central leaf stalks which may extend slightly beyond the tip of the leaf, [[dioicy]], and long stems densely matted with [[rhizoid]]s. It is found worldwide, excluding the [[tropics]].

==Description==
''Ptychstomum pseudotriquem'' is a medium to large<ref name="tropicos">{{cite web |title=!''Bryum pseudotriquetrum'' (Hedw.) G. Gaertn., B. Mey. & Scherb. |url=http://legacy.tropicos.org/NamePage.aspx?nameid=35152064&projectid=41 |website=[[Tropicos]] |publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]] |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> moss with an [[Bryopsida #Morphological groups|acrocarpous]] growth form.<ref name="british">{{cite web |title=''Bryum pseudotriquetrum'' |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/learning/species-finder/bryum-pseudotriquetrum/ |website=[[British Bryological Society]] |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> It is a yellow-green<ref name="tropicos"/> moss that becomes red-brown with age.<ref name="fna">{{cite web |last1=Spence |first1=John R. |title=Ptychostomum pseudotriquetrum |url=https://floranorthamerica.org/Ptychostomum_pseudotriquetrum |website=Flora of North America |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> The stems occur in dense turfs. The stems usually grow to lengths of 2–4{{nbsp}}cm<ref name="fna"/> but can be as short as 1{{nbsp}}cm and long as 6{{nbsp}}cm.<ref name="tropicos"/> The stems may be weakly comose (i.e. crowned with a tuft of soft leaves) or evenly foliate.<ref name="fna"/> The lower part of the stem is matted with papillose red-brown [[rhizoid]]s.<ref name="tropicos"/><ref name="aussie">{{cite web |last1=Spence |first1=John R. |last2=Ramsay |first2=Helen P. |title=Ptychostomum |url=https://www.anbg.gov.au/abrs/Mosses_online/Bryaceae_Ptychostomum.pdf |website=Australian Mosses Online |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> The stems branch sparingly by means of subfloral innovations,<ref name="aussie"/> which are elongate and evenly foliate.<ref name="fna"/>

The leaves typically measure 2–3{{nbsp}}mm in length, but may as short as 1{{nbsp}}mm or as long as 4{{nbsp}}mm.<ref name="fna"/> The leaves are glossy<ref name="british"/> and green, red-green, or yellow-green when young. They become dull brown-red or brick-red with age.<ref name="fna"/> They are twisted and contorted when dry. When moist, they are erect spreading, oblong‑lanceolate to ovate‑lanceolate,<ref name="tropicos"/> and flat to weakly concave. This means that the leaves are widest near the base and taper to a point. The leaves' cell walls are firm to incrassate<ref name="fna"/> and sometimes porose.<ref name="tropicos"/> The reddish<ref name="aussie"/> basal cells are rectangular. The distal cells are rhomboidal-hexagonal to hexagonal,<ref name="tropicos"/> with a length of 20–40{{nbsp}}μm and a width of 12–20{{nbsp}}μm.<ref name="aussie"/> The leaves are bordered by 2–3 rows of narrow, thick-walled, usually red cells.<ref name="tropicos"/> The leaf margins are revolute (i.e. rolled downward) from the base of the blade to the middle of the leaf or further.<ref name="fna"/> Near the apex, the leaf margins are denticulate (i.e. having fine teeth).<ref name="aussie"/> The stout red-brown costa, or central stalk of the leaf, is percurrent to slightly excurrent, meaning it extends beyond the end of the apex,<ref name="aussie"/><ref name="tropicos"/> ending in a smooth [[awn (botany)|awn]]. The leaf base is narrow and strongly [[decurrent]], extending far down the stem.<ref name="fna"/>

Some populations in the [[Northern Hemisphere]]<ref name="aussie"/> can reproduce asexually by means of brown [[gemma (botany)|gemma]]e in the leaf axils.<ref name="fna"/> The plants are [[Dioicy|dioicous]], having male and female sexual organs on separate plants.<ref name="fna"/> The [[seta]], or capsule stalk, is usually 1–3{{nbsp}}cm long, though infrequently as long as 4{{nbsp}}cm.<ref name="fna"/> The seta is red, becoming browner with age.<ref name="tropicos"/> The capsule, which contains the [[spore]]s, is 3–5{{nbsp}}mm long and brown but with a yellow mouth.<ref name="fna"/> The capsule is thickened at its distal end, with its shape being variously described as "elongate-ovate" (i.e. having an elongated egg shape),<ref name="fna"/> "cylindrical to clavate" (i.e. club-shaped),<ref name="tropicos"/> and "broadly pyriform" (i.e. pear-shaped).<ref name="aussie"/> It is either pendulous or inclined.<ref name="brit2">{{cite web |last1=Lawley |first1=Mark |last2=Graham |first2=Jonathan |last3=Holyoak |first3=David |title=''Bryum pseudotriquetrum'' |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Bryum-pseudotriquetrum.pdf |website=[[British Bryological Society]] |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> The diplolepidous [[peristome]] is composed of two sets of teeth, an inner endostome and an outer exostome, which ring the mouth of the capsule. The exostome teeth are orange-<ref name="aussie"/> or yellow-brown to pale yellow<ref name="tropicos"/> and papillose at the tips.<ref name="aussie"/> The yellowish hyaline (i.e. translucent) endostome teeth are lightly papillose,<ref name="tropicos"/> have broad perforations, and have a membrane at the base that is half the height of the exostome teeth. Attached to the endostome cells are 2–3 long, filiform (i.e. threadlike), appendiculate [[cilia]].<ref name="aussie"/><ref name="fna"/> The [[Operculum (botany)|operculum]] (the cap of the capsule) is 0.5–0.8{{nbsp}}mm long and conic-apiculate, ending in a sharp point.<ref name="tropicos"/> The pale yellow or green spores measure 12–18{{nbsp}}μm in diameter and are finely papillose.<ref name="fna"/> The capsules mature in the summer or fall,<ref name="brit2"/> in the Northern Hemisphere from April to October.<ref name="fna"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Bryum pseudotriquetrum'' is a synonym of ''Ptychostomum pseudotriquetrum''.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Bryum pseudotriquetrum'' (Hedw.) P. Gaertn., B. Mey. & Scherb. |url=http://www.worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-0001176868 |website=[[World Flora Online]] |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref>

''[[Ptychostomum bimum]]'' has historically been treated as a synoicous form of ''Ptychostomum pseudotriquetrum''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Spence |first1=John R. |title=Ptychostomum bimum |url=https://floranorthamerica.org/Ptychostomum_bimum |website=Flora of North America |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> ''P. bimum'' has twice as many [[chromosome]]s as and probably evolved from ''P. pseudotriquetrum''<ref name="sweden">{{cite web |last1=Sjölander |first1=Isabell |title=A comparative study of the mosses ''Ptychostomum pseudotriquetrum'' and ''P. bimum'' |url=https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:1736166/FULLTEXT01.pdf |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> As of June 2024, [[World Flora Online]] treats the two species as separate.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ptychostomum Hornsch. |url=https://wfoplantlist.org/taxon/wfo-4000032141-2024-06?page=1 |website=[[World Flora Online]] |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> Compared to ''P. pseudotriquetrum'', ''P. bimum'' has a shorter stem and significantly shorter leaf decurrencies.<ref name="fna"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''P. pseudotriquetrum'' has a bipolar distribution and is additionally found in [[temperate]] regions in the [[Southern Hemisphere]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Ptychostomum pseudotriquetrum'' (Hedw.) J.R.Spence & H.P.Ramsay ex Holyoak & N.Pedersen |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/7459211 |website=[[Global Biodiversity Information Facility]] |access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref> It is found on all continents, including [[Antarctica]],<ref name="aussie"/> but is largely absent from the [[tropics]], [[subtropics]], and islands in the central [[Pacific Ocean]].<ref name="fna"/> It grows on rocks and wet soil<ref name="aussie"/> by streams and lakes<ref name="sweden"/> and in fens, wet heaths, and marshes. at elevations of 0–4000{{nbsp}}m.<ref name="fna"/>
